record.original_question: Define Donaldson–Thomas invariants for varieties of dimension greater than 3. The motivating issue stated in the paper is that the usual definition in dimension 3 depends on having a virtual fundamental class for a moduli space of sheaves, with deformations controlled by Ext^1(E,E), obstructions by Ext^2(E,E), and a needed vanishing of Ext^i(E,E) for i > 2; the problem asks for an analogue beyond the 3-dimensional setting.

evidence.quote: Donaldson–Thomas invariants are defined only in dimension 3 because a virtual fundamental class for the moduli space of sheaves is required. Deformations are given by Ext1(E, E), obstructions by Ext2(E, E), and to define the virtual fundamental class we need (roughly) the vanishing Exti(E, E) = 0 for i > 2 .
Q5. Define Donaldson–Thomas invariants in dimensions > 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let X be a smooth projective Calabi–Yau threefold, and let M be a moduli space of stable coherent sheaves E on X. The Donaldson–Thomas (DT) invariants of X are integers obtained by integration against a virtual fundamental class [M]^vir on M. The construction relies on the two-term obstruction theory in which infinitesimal deformations of a sheaf E are governed by Ext^1(E,E), obstructions by Ext^2(E,E), and the higher groups Ext^i(E,E) with i > 2 are required (roughly) to vanish, so that the moduli problem admits a perfect obstruction theory and a virtual class.

Problem. Construct a theory of Donaldson–Thomas-type invariants for moduli spaces of stable sheaves on smooth projective varieties X of complex dimension strictly greater than 3. Specifically:

(a) Identify a class of higher-dimensional varieties X (e.g. with prescribed canonical bundle and Calabi–Yau-type conditions) for which a well-defined deformation-invariant enumerative theory of sheaves can be constructed.

(b) Define a virtual fundamental class (or a substitute) on the moduli space of stable sheaves on X in such a setting, dealing with the failure of the vanishing Ext^i(E,E) = 0 for i > 2 that holds in the threefold case.

(c) Use this construction to define numerical invariants generalizing DT invariants beyond dimension 3, and establish their basic properties (deformation invariance, wall-crossing behaviour, and relations to other enumerative invariants where applicable).
artifact.status_search_result: For Calabi–Yau 4-folds, a definition of DT-type invariants (DT4 invariants) was given by Borisov–Joyce (2015) using shifted symplectic derived algebraic geometry (PTVV) and derived differential geometry, with subsequent algebraic constructions and extensive development by Cao–Leung, Oh–Thomas, and others. So the dimension-4 case is now broadly addressed. A complete general theory in arbitrary dimension > 4 (and for non-Calabi–Yau higher-dimensional varieties) is not established, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Calabi–Yau manifolds: Donaldson–Thomas invariants (Joyce handout)
status_evidence.snippet: DT-type invariants for Calabi–Yau 4-folds defined via shifted symplectic derived schemes (PTVV) and derived differential geometry; virtual cycle constructed by Borisov–Joyce.
status_evidence.claim: DT invariants for CY 4-folds were defined by Borisov–Joyce, addressing the dimension-4 case of the problem.

status_evidence.title: Donaldson–Thomas theory for Calabi–Yau four-folds
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs DT-type invariants counting stable sheaves on CY 4-folds; the virtual class is no longer of degree zero, so insertions are needed.
status_evidence.claim: Mathematical theory of DT invariants on CY 4-folds has been developed, partially solving the higher-dimensional question.
